content.text:
I submitted **index 84** (Bi 0.08, Cu 0.55, V 0.37) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 2.6e-7 A.

The light is 2.06 eV, which is below BiVO4's band gap (~2.4 eV), so the Bi-rich BiVO4 region should absorb little. I focused instead on copper vanadates, which have smaller band gaps (~1.8–2.0 eV). I used all 3 merit measurements along the copper-to-vanadium ratio, with bismuth held low (about 8%):

| Index | Cu:V ratio | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | ~0.87 (more vanadium) | 6e-8 |
| **84** | **~1.5 (close to Cu3V2O8)** | **2.6e-7** |
| 101 | ~2.3 (more copper) | 1.3e-7 |

Photocurrent rose, then fell, so the best composition along this line is probably near a Cu:V ratio of 1.5. Index 84 may still not be the library's best. Three points leave the curve's shape poorly defined, and I never varied the bismuth content. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. They wouldn't have helped once the merit budget was spent, since only compositions with a measured photocurrent count toward the score.
